findings.reason: Verified in dualwriter_mode3.go that the async goroutines derive their context from the request ctx via WithTimeoutCause, so they are cancelled when the handler returns; Mode 1 shares the pattern, but the Mode 3 legacy copy is the fallback here.
Confirmed the new goroutines at lines 55-56, 112-113, 139-140 and 165-166 only pass errObjectSt/err into a duration metric and never log it, while the old code logged legacy failures.

Confirmed line 45 and line 129 call recordLegacyDuration for unified-store errors, line 166 calls recordStorageDuration for the legacy result, and line 106 passes name where options.Kind is used everywhere else.

Confirmed the old code wrapped objInfo in updateWrapper with the unified-store result, and the new Update passes the raw objInfo to Legacy.Update, which changes what legacy applies and can diverge the stores.
Confirmed the old Delete ignored IsNotFound from storage and still deleted from legacy, while the new code returns early on any storage error, so legacy-only objects are no longer removed.

Mode 1 DeepCopies before its goroutine and Mode 3 passes the shared obj, so a legacy mutation of metadata could race with the handler reading the returned object; the race is plausible but not shown concretely.
Confirmed line 97 attaches d.Log rather than the enriched log, dropping name/kind/method from the context; this is a readability and consistency issue with little behavioural impact.

Verified the tests share one mock.Mock for legacy and storage, never await or assert the async legacy calls, and have misleading names, so they would pass without the dual write, though this is mostly a test-quality gap.
